newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Islamic Jihad memorial draws hundreds in Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Islamic Jihad memorial draws hundreds in Gaza.

text.p: Hundreds of Palestinians from all political factions in Gaza attended a rally on Saturday to mark the first anniversary of the assassination of Fathi Shqaqi, leader of the militant Islamic Jihad group.

"There is a conspiracy today to split the Palestinian people...through a series of political assassinations," Hani al-Hassan, a close adviser to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, told the gathering in a Gaza City cultural centre.

"I am greatly concerned at this stage with the security of President Arafat because they know that by attacking him, sedition will ensue and the Israeli line will be imposed," Hassan said, without naming any "conspirators".
Shqaqi was shot dead in Malta a year ago. His assassins were never found but Israel's Mossad secret service is widely believed to be behind the killing.
Islamic Jihad, which opposes the Israel-PLO peace deals and carried out suicide attacks in the Jewish state, has vowed to avenge his death.
Israel sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip on Thursday in response to what an army spokesman said were numerous warnings of revenge attacks by the group.
Shqaqi's father, brother and leaders of the militant Moslem organisation Hamas and factions of the Palestine Liberation Organisation were among the 700 people who attended the rally.
Arafat and ministers of the Palestinian self-rule Authority were not present but members of the Palestinians Legislative Council and the Executive Committee of the PLO did attend.

In a message read at the rally, Shqaqi's successor, Ramadan Abdallah Shallah, who is said to live between Lebanon and Syria, wrote: "The Israeli enemy should not forget for a minute that all the world knows that all of Palestine is ours. We will not concede a single metre."
At Bir Zeit University in the West Bank, hundreds of students marched through the campus and heard speeches commemorating Shqaqi.
